title: How to talk about your family tree in English🌳🤗: Real Easy English

sentences.en: Hello, I'm Phil.
sentences.ko: 안녕하세요, 저는 필이에요.

sentences.en: And I'm Georgie.
sentences.ko: 그리고 저는 조지예요.

sentences.en: Welcome to Real Easy English.
sentences.ko: Real Easy English에 오신 걸 환영해요.

sentences.en: Remember, you can find the vocabulary from this episode and test yourself with a free worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.ko: 기억하세요, 이 에피소드의 어휘와 무료 학습지는 웹사이트 bbclearningenglish.com에서 볼 수 있어요.

sentences.en: Hi Georgie, how are you?
sentences.ko: 안녕, 조지, 잘 지내요?

sentences.en: I'm very well, thank you, Phil. How are you?
sentences.ko: 아주 잘 지내요, 고마워요, 필. 당신은요?

sentences.en: I'm really good.
sentences.ko: 정말 잘 지내요.

sentences.en: Today we're going to talk about our families and particularly our extended families.
sentences.ko: 오늘은 가족, 특히 친척(extended family)에 대해 얘기해 볼게요.

sentences.en: Georgie, do you have a big family?
sentences.ko: 조지, 가족이 많아요?

sentences.en: I don't actually.
sentences.ko: 사실 아니에요.

sentences.en: I have my two parents, a sister and then outside of that, my family is quite small.
sentences.ko: 부모님 두 분과 여동생이 있고, 그 밖의 가족은 꽤 적어요.

sentences.en: I've got one aunt, two uncles, and only one of my uncles has children, so I don't have many cousins. What about you?
sentences.ko: 이모(고모)가 한 명, 삼촌이 두 명인데, 삼촌 중 한 명만 자녀가 있어서 사촌이 많지 않아요. 당신은요?

sentences.en: Do you have a big family?
sentences.ko: 가족이 많아요?

sentences.en: Actually, my family is probably similar. I've got...
sentences.ko: 사실 저희 가족도 비슷할 거예요. 저는...

sentences.en: I've got a brother, and then I've got two aunts, three uncles.
sentences.ko: 형제가 한 명 있고, 이모(고모)가 두 명, 삼촌이 세 명 있어요.

sentences.en: I've got...
sentences.ko: 그리고...

sentences.en: Well, I've got three cousins that I know and a cousin somewhere lost in Australia.
sentences.ko: 음, 아는 사촌이 세 명 있고, 호주 어딘가에 연락이 끊긴 사촌이 한 명 있어요.

sentences.en: Oh wow! Interesting.
sentences.ko: 오 와! 흥미롭네요.

sentences.en: So, we both have quite small extended families.
sentences.ko: 그러니까 우리 둘 다 친척이 꽤 적네요.

sentences.en: Do you see yours much?
sentences.ko: 친척들 자주 봐요?

sentences.en: Usually only at times, like at Christmas, I'll often see especially my uncles and my aunts.
sentences.ko: 보통 크리스마스 같은 때만요. 특히 삼촌들과 이모(고모)들을 자주 봐요.

sentences.en: I see them fairly regularly.
sentences.ko: 꽤 정기적으로 봐요.

sentences.en: My cousins – yeah, often Christmas or New Year or something like that.
sentences.ko: 사촌들은, 네, 주로 크리스마스나 새해 같은 때요.

sentences.en: Same with me, really.
sentences.ko: 저도 정말 똑같아요.

sentences.en: Growing up, my uncle, who has children who are my cousins, they lived quite far away, so it was similar.
sentences.ko: 어렸을 때, 제 사촌들의 아빠인 삼촌네가 꽤 멀리 살아서 비슷했어요.

sentences.en: We only really saw them at Christmas and times like that.
sentences.ko: 크리스마스 같은 때만 봤어요.

sentences.en: And nowadays I only really see my extended family at events like weddings and, sadly, funerals.
sentences.ko: 그리고 요즘은 결혼식이나, 안타깝지만 장례식 같은 행사에서만 친척들을 봐요.

sentences.en: I'd probably like to see them more.
sentences.ko: 더 자주 보고 싶긴 해요.

sentences.en: But this is life.
sentences.ko: 그래도 그게 인생이죠.

sentences.en: OK. Georgie, what about your grandparents?
sentences.ko: 그렇군요. 조지, 조부모님은요?

sentences.en: Have you been close with your grandparents?
sentences.ko: 조부모님과 가까웠어요?

sentences.en: Yeah. So, sadly, I don't have any grandparents left.
sentences.ko: 네. 안타깝게도 조부모님은 이제 아무도 안 계세요.

sentences.en: They've all died, but I was really close with particularly my grandmothers.
sentences.ko: 다 돌아가셨는데, 특히 할머니들과 정말 가까웠어요.

sentences.en: Both of them lived quite close to me, so that was really nice.
sentences.ko: 두 분 다 저희 집과 꽤 가까이 사셔서 정말 좋았어요.

sentences.en: I could spend a lot of time with them.
sentences.ko: 함께 많은 시간을 보낼 수 있었어요.

sentences.en: They were big personalities – really funny, really loving, caring.
sentences.ko: 두 분 다 개성이 강하셨어요. 정말 재밌고, 다정하고, 자상하셨어요.

sentences.en: And yeah, I was really close with them. What about you?
sentences.ko: 네, 정말 가까웠어요. 당신은요?

sentences.en: Yeah, I think for me it's kind of similar to your story, really.
sentences.ko: 네, 저도 당신 얘기랑 정말 비슷한 것 같아요.

sentences.en: I don't have any grandparents now, but when I was younger, the two grandparents that were still alive then, I was quite close to.
sentences.ko: 지금은 조부모님이 안 계시지만, 어렸을 때 살아 계셨던 두 분과 꽤 가까웠어요.

sentences.en: I used to see my granddad every week.
sentences.ko: 할아버지를 매주 뵀어요.

sentences.en: He used to come and do the shopping for my mum, and I'd see my grandma quite regularly as well.
sentences.ko: 할아버지가 오셔서 엄마 대신 장을 봐 주셨고, 할머니도 꽤 자주 뵀어요.

sentences.en: Yeah, I was quite close with them when I was younger.
sentences.ko: 네, 어렸을 때 꽤 가까웠어요.

sentences.en: To talk about our extended families, we often look at family trees.
sentences.ko: 친척에 대해 얘기할 때 가계도(family tree)를 자주 봐요.

sentences.en: That's like a diagram that shows your family history.
sentences.ko: 가족의 역사를 보여 주는 도표 같은 거예요.

sentences.en: Have you researched your family tree?
sentences.ko: 가계도를 조사해 본 적 있어요?

sentences.en: I personally haven't researched my family tree, but other people in my family have researched it quite a lot, so I can see the bits of my family going back lots of generations – going back to Scotland, to Ireland, to Norway,
sentences.ko: 저는 직접 해 본 적 없지만, 가족 중 다른 사람들이 꽤 많이 조사해서 여러 세대 거슬러 올라가는 우리 가족을 볼 수 있어요. 스코틀랜드, 아일랜드, 노르웨이,

sentences.en: to Armenia and places like this.
sentences.ko: 아르메니아 같은 곳까지요.

sentences.en: Wow. So, your ancestors are from all over the world, it sounds like?
sentences.ko: 와. 그러니까 조상이 전 세계 곳곳에서 왔네요?

sentences.en: Quite a few places, yeah.
sentences.ko: 꽤 여러 곳이요, 네.

sentences.en: Yeah, I also have not researched my family tree, but I really would like to because I do know that my great grandmother was Italian and my great grandfather was from the US,
sentences.ko: 네, 저도 가계도를 조사해 본 적은 없는데, 정말 해 보고 싶어요. 증조할머니가 이탈리아 사람이고 증조할아버지가 미국 출신이라는 건 알거든요.

sentences.en: so I would love to, kind of, find some family members from those countries and maybe become close with them.
sentences.ko: 그래서 그 나라들에서 친척을 찾아서 가까워지고 싶어요.

sentences.en: I think that would be really interesting to, kind of, understand more about my history.
sentences.ko: 제 뿌리에 대해 더 이해하는 게 정말 흥미로울 것 같아요.

sentences.en: If you want to know more about your family history, I think you can often look it up.
sentences.ko: 가족의 역사에 대해 더 알고 싶으면 보통 찾아볼(look it up) 수 있어요.

sentences.en: You can... you can look it up in records in government offices, but also I think there's a lot of websites where you can look things up now and find...
sentences.ko: 정부 기관 기록에서 찾아볼 수도 있고, 요즘은 찾아볼 수 있는 웹사이트도 많은 것 같아요.

sentences.en: find out your family history – find out about your ancestors.
sentences.ko: 가족의 역사, 조상에 대해 알아볼 수 있죠.

sentences.en: Yes. Well, actually, there is a story that my family tells that I'm not sure is true, but one of my ancestors apparently has a connection to royalty – a big event in history.
sentences.ko: 네. 사실 저희 가족이 하는 이야기가 있는데 사실인지는 잘 모르겠어요. 조상 중 한 명이 왕실과 연관이 있다고 해요. 역사적으로 큰 사건이요.

sentences.en: But again, I don't know if it's true, so I'd love to look it up and find out the facts.
sentences.ko: 그런데 역시 사실인지 모르니까, 찾아보고 진실을 알아내고 싶어요.

sentences.en: I think that would be good.
sentences.ko: 그거 좋겠네요.

sentences.en: OK. Let's recap the vocabulary that we've looked at in this episode, starting with 'close'.
sentences.ko: 좋아요. 이번 에피소드에서 본 어휘를 정리해 봐요. 'close'부터요.

sentences.en: If you're 'close with' or 'close to' a family member, then it's someone whom you see a lot and you get on well with.
sentences.ko: 가족 중 누군가와 'close with' 또는 'close to'하다면, 자주 보고 사이가 좋은 사람이라는 뜻이에요.

sentences.en: Your 'family tree' is a diagram or image which shows your family history.
sentences.ko: 'family tree'는 가족의 역사를 보여 주는 도표나 그림이에요.

sentences.en: Your 'ancestors' are your relatives from a long time ago.
sentences.ko: 'ancestors'는 아주 오래전의 친척들, 즉 조상이에요.

sentences.en: Lots of people like to look up their ancestors.
sentences.ko: 많은 사람이 자기 조상을 찾아보는 걸 좋아해요.

sentences.en: If you 'look something up', you try to find out information – for example, by searching online or reading books.
sentences.ko: 뭔가를 'look up'하면 정보를 알아보려고 하는 거예요. 예를 들어 인터넷 검색이나 책을 통해서요.

sentences.en: That's it for this episode of Real Easy English.
sentences.ko: Real Easy English 이번 에피소드는 여기까지예요.

sentences.en: We'll be back next week with another episode in easy English.
sentences.ko: 다음 주에 쉬운 영어로 된 다른 에피소드로 돌아올게요.

sentences.en: And if you want to learn to talk more about your family, we have a collection of episodes all about this topic.
sentences.ko: 그리고 가족에 대해 더 말하는 법을 배우고 싶으면, 이 주제만 모은 에피소드 모음이 있어요.

sentences.en: Go to bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.ko: bbclearningenglish.com에 가 보세요.

sentences.en: Bye for now!
sentences.ko: 오늘은 여기까지, 안녕!

sentences.en: Goodbye!
sentences.ko: 안녕!
